findings.reason: §2's measured curve is the summed error (ε² model error plus rounding-over-ε), sampled at each slope's own optimal ε, so the rounding term at the production width is neither recorded nor separable from it, and the §3 worker has no number for the clause and must either guess a tolerance or fail the node.
findings.text: done-when (1) is measured to within "the largest per-slope rounding term §2 records at the production strip width", but §2 (line 215-219) records only the best attainable error and its ε per slope, and the single production fraction, never a rounding term at that width

findings.reason: read literally, the first run writes no cache entry and the second run misses, so the clause is unsatisfiable by the two runs it names; it needs one line saying the first run populates the cache (or that "disabled" means cleared, not off) for the worker to satisfy clause (2) at all.
findings.text: done-when (2) fixes the cost measurement to "fresh process and persistent cache disabled" and then requires "a second run hitting the persistent cache" in the same clause, which describes a cache that the first run was told not to write
